vibe: Model-price war goes nuclear while security AIs get so good at finding bugs their makers won't ship the weights.

cyber.title: Slovakia finds Russian-made backdoor in national traffic speed cameras
cyber.summary: Slovak authorities discovered undocumented remote-access functionality in Russian-supplied traffic enforcement cameras — a textbook hardware supply-chain risk in critical public infrastructure, and a reminder to audit the provenance of edge devices.

cyber.title: Lazarus exploits a Windows zero-day to gain SYSTEM access and drop a backdoor
cyber.summary: North Korea's Lazarus group chained a privilege-escalation zero-day to land SYSTEM and deploy a stealth backdoor. Confirm your August Windows patches are actually deployed, not just downloaded.

cyber.title: ToxicPanda Android malware abuses VPN permissions to block Google Play Protect
cyber.summary: The banking trojan sets up a local VPN so it can silently cut Play Protect's connection and stay resident — a clever survival trick worth knowing if you manage any Android fleet.

ai.title: Z.ai's open GLM-5.3 found 1,000+ real security bugs — so they're holding the weights back ~2 weeks
ai.summary: Z.ai's new open coding model surfaced over a thousand genuine vulnerabilities in software like Linux and WebKit during training — its offensive-security skill grew faster than planned, so the company is delaying the public weights and shipping an 'OpenVuln' scanner instead. The AI-finds-bugs era just got real.

ai.title: OpenAI paused training after a model neared its highest cybersecurity-risk tier
ai.summary: OpenAI disclosed a two-week training pause after a frontier model approached the top of its own cyber-risk scale — landing the same week Wiz's autonomous 'Red Agent' found and exploited a real GitHub Actions flaw in a Snowflake repo. Frontier models are crossing into serious offensive capability.

ai.title: Anthropic watermarks Claude output for the EU AI Act — a Paris dev's open-source tool already strips it
ai.summary: Anthropic began embedding invisible machine-readable watermarks in Claude's output to meet EU AI Act provenance rules; within days a developer released an open tool that removes them. The AI-provenance cat-and-mouse is off and running.

ai.title: The model price war goes nuclear — and Anthropic's flagship reportedly struggles for users
ai.summary: OpenAI cut GPT-5.6 Sol pricing 20%+, Google shipped Gemini 3.7 Flash at half the prior tier, DeepSeek V4-Pro and Qwen3.8-Max landed — and the FT reports Anthropic's best model is struggling to attract users against cheaper rivals. Good news if you're paying for tokens.

ai.title: Twitch and Amazon sued for training AI on streamers' content
ai.summary: A new lawsuit alleges Amazon used creators' Twitch content to train AI without consent — another front in the escalating fight over training-data rights.

ai.title: Vercel ships 'Is Agentic', a free tool that scores how agent-ready your website is
ai.summary: Vercel's free auditor runs ~100 checks on a public site and grades how easily AI agents can read and act on it — a peek at where 'agent SEO' is heading.

it.title: AWS and Google Cloud expand a joint multicloud collaboration
it.summary: The two hyperscalers are making it easier to wire their platforms together for multicloud deployments, with Azure slated to join. Relevant if any of your architectures straddle providers.

videos.title: What Is a Digital Librarian AI Agent? Connecting SQL & Vector Databases
videos.verdict: SKIM — the architecture pattern is the payoff; watch the 6-step walkthrough, skip the pharmacy framing
videos.summary: A clean explainer on building an agent that routes a question into two worlds — the 'what' (a precise SQL query against structured data) and the 'why' (semantic search over unstructured PDFs in a vector DB) — then compiles both into one grounded answer. A tidy mental model for anyone wiring RAG onto real enterprise data.
